sections.admission_summary: Chief complaint: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea. Admitted for inpatient care.
sections.discharge_instructions: Drink plenty of fluids. Get adequate rest and avoid overexertion. Cardiology follow-up within 1-2 weeks. Cardiac rehabilitation enrollment recommended. Take your heart medications (Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Atorvastatin) every day as prescribed. Do NOT stop them without consulting your cardiologist. Call 911 immediately for: chest pain, severe shortness of breath, palpitations, syncope. Resume a normal diet gradually as tolerated. Restricted activity for 4-6 weeks. Avoid heavy lifting. Gradual return per cardiologist guidance. Call ambulance immediately for chest pain lasting >15 min, dyspnea, syncope, or cold sweats. Low-fat, low-sodium diet. Weight management.
sections.discharge_medications: Aspirin 81mg PO daily; Ticagrelor 90mg PO BID; Atorvastatin 80mg PO daily
sections.follow_up: Cardiology follow-up within 1-2 weeks. Cardiac rehabilitation enrollment recommended.
sections.hospital_course: Length of stay: 14 days (primary reason: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea). Main treatment: vasoactive drugs (Norepinephrine, Dobutamine); anticoagulation (Heparin); insulin (Insulin, Regular, Human); analgesia (Aspirin); other parenteral drugs (Nitroglycerin, Calcium Gluconate). Key procedures: Urinary catheter insertion (2024-06-15), Arterial line insertion (2024-06-15), Transthoracic echocardiography (2024-06-15), Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (2024-06-15). Significant results: troponin I 97.882 ng/mL [H] (prior 68.499; troponin elevation) on hospital day 1; creatinine 2.94 mg/dL [H] (prior 2.72; AKI by KDIGO criteria) on hospital day 12. Medication changes from admission: started Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Atorvastatin. Condition at discharge: discharged to skilled nursing facility, Barthel Index 95/100.
